problem.title: Unreviewed thinking becomes mental noise.
problem.body: Most high-performers do not need more input. They need a way to review the thinking already running in the background: decisions, assumptions, pressure, emotional residue, and repeated loops.
points: Unfinished decisions stay open and consume attention.
Facts, feelings, assumptions, and imagined outcomes blend together.
Judgment gets weaker when thinking has not been reviewed.

method.title: Red Pen Thought Review™
method.body: This is not journaling for self-discovery alone. It is a structured thought review method: write what is occupying mental space, mark what carries weight, separate fact from story, and choose one clearer next move.

steps.title: Empty
steps.text: Externalize the thoughts, pressures, loops, and decisions currently occupying mental space.

steps.title: Mark
steps.text: Use the red pen to identify repeated themes, charged words, vague language, and unresolved decisions.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: Distinguish fact, feeling, and story so not every thought is treated as equally true.

steps.title: Decide
steps.text: Name the real decision or the question to carry forward, then choose one specific next move.

redPen.title: The red pen is the review layer.
redPen.body: Red is not decoration. It signals review, annotation, correction, and distance. Changing pen colour switches you from expression to observation, so you can see your thinking from the outside before deciding what to do next.

aiEra.title: AI gives you answers. Red Pen helps you review the question.
aiEra.body: AI can generate endless output. It cannot tell you which assumption is driving your reaction, which story you are repeating, or which decision you are avoiding. Red Pen Thought Review creates a deliberate pause between input and judgment.
